explained.headline: Democrats win control of US Congress in midterm elections

happened.text: Democratic Party candidates secured control of both the US Senate and the House of Representatives in the midterm elections.
Voters delivered a stinging rebuke to President Donald Trump and his party, handing Democrats victories in several states that had previously been reliably Republican.
The election also featured a series of historic firsts, including the election of Abdul El-Sayed as the first Muslim US senator.

background.text: The elections took place halfway through Donald Trump's second term, following his return to the White House in January 2025 with unified Republican control of Congress.
In the preceding months, the Trump administration had pursued sometimes unpopular policies on trade and immigration while launching a war against Iran.

matters.text: The Democratic majorities in Congress will enable the party to frustrate Donald Trump's legislative agenda and launch investigations into his administration.
Donald Trump acknowledged that his party's poor performance was likely impacted by the short-term consequences of the war on Iran, particularly regarding gasoline prices.

uncertain.text: It remains to be seen whether Donald Trump will adjust his approach or seek to strike deals with congressional Democrats during his final two years in office.
Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated in a written message that expectations of a genuine shift in US policy toward Tehran were mistaken, leaving the future of bilateral hostility unclear.

explained.headline: Israel Election Commission Rejects Fraud Claims as Consultations Begin

happened.text: Israel's election commission certified the final results of the 27 October vote, rejecting claims of mass fraud promoted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
The election authorities presented the final results to President Isaac Herzog, who began consultations with party leaders on forming a government.
The attorney general blocked a demand from the Shin Bet security service to interrogate senior politicians from Palestinian-led parties due to a lack of evidence.

background.text: Neither Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot attained the 61 seats needed to govern, while Arab-led parties secured a record 19 seats.
Isaac Herzog plays a crucial role in forming the next government by choosing which politician has the first chance to create a coalition.

matters.text: Analyst Nadav Eyal warned that Israelis should brace for more extreme attempts to dismiss election results and discredit leading opposition parties.
Gadi Eisenkot warned of ongoing attempts to undermine trust in the election results and accused Benjamin Netanyahu of weaponising security services.
Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg stated that those casting doubt on the election results pose a real danger to Israel's democracy.

uncertain.text: It remains to be seen how long coalition negotiations will take, with observers expecting weeks of tough talks.
The election committee noted that some suspicions were still under investigation, though they do not cast doubt on the election as a whole.
It is still uncertain whether Arab-led parties will recommend either candidate for prime minister or under what conditions.

explained.headline: South Africans vote in local elections amid declining support for ANC

happened.text: South Africans began voting in municipal elections on Wednesday that could lead to fresh losses for the governing African National Congress.
The vote takes place amid rising frustration over failing public services, including unreliable water and electricity supplies, high crime rates, and unemployment.
Election officials stated that voting was proceeding smoothly despite long queues at certain polling stations.

background.text: The African National Congress is the former liberation movement led by Nelson Mandela that has governed South Africa since the end of apartheid in 1994.
The party lost its parliamentary majority for the first time in the 2024 national elections, subsequently entering a national coalition with the Democratic Alliance and several other parties.

matters.text: Analysts suggest that further declines in support will lead to more municipalities being governed by unstable and chaotic coalition arrangements.

uncertain.text: It remains unclear whether the uMkhonto weSizwe Party will secure an outright majority in the eThekwini metro area.
Political analyst Dr Levy Ndou stated uncertainty over whether the national unity government arrangement could influence how municipalities are eventually run.

explained.headline: Canada joins ice hockey boycott as Ukraine talks proceed in Berlin

happened.text: Canada has joined a coalition of nations refusing to play ice hockey against Russian teams, meaning Russian skaters cannot compete in an upcoming world junior championship in Canada.
Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met in Berlin to discuss ceasefire negotiations and security guarantees.
Russian airstrikes on a school building and a hospital in Ukraine killed and injured numerous civilians.

background.text: The sports dispute arose after the Court of Arbitration for Sport lifted an International Ice Hockey Federation ban on Russian teams that had been in place since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began.
Several national hockey federations subsequently announced they would refuse to play matches involving Russia to protect player safety and uphold sporting values.
On the diplomatic front, Germany has been a key supporter of Ukraine, providing aid and prioritizing air defense and energy infrastructure ahead of winter.

matters.text: Norwegian officials stated that playing against Russia could expose players and team staff to significant security risks.
Zelenskyy stated that a ceasefire alone would not secure lasting peace, and that Ukraine requires robust security guarantees backed by Europe and the United States.
Merz warned that ongoing Russian attacks in the Black Sea risk further escalation and precipitate a global food crisis detrimental to the world's poorest nations.

uncertain.text: It remains to be seen whether upcoming international tournaments will proceed as planned or how host cities will decide to handle the participation of Russian athletes.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated he sees no indication that Russia is genuinely prepared to engage in serious negotiations regarding a ceasefire.
Uncertainty also surrounds the exact level of future financial support and whether European representatives will secure a meaningful seat at upcoming US-led talks in Abu Dhabi.
